verdict.rationale: Greptile's docs describe iterating on a PR until it gives a perfect review with zero unresolved comments, distinguishing unaddressed feedback, and skipping repetitive feedback. Together these imply re-reviews that track resolution. However, no evidence states that a new commit push automatically triggers an incremental, diff-only re-review that marks prior comments as fixed. missing for 10: explicit documentation of push-triggered incremental re-review scoped to new commits, explicit fixed-comment tracking or de-duplication across review rounds, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, pushing new commits triggers an incremental re-review that tracks what was fixed instead of repeating old comments

citations.quote: Iteratively fix a PR until Greptile gives a perfect review: 5/5 confidence, zero unresolved comments.
Fetch PR comments - Get unaddressed Greptile feedback for any PR
With noise control, Greptile limits reviews to high-signal insights, skipping low impact or repetitive feedback.
